newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taipei OKs ADB T$7 bln Taiwan-dollar bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Taipei OKs ADB T$7 bln Taiwan-dollar bond issue.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Thursday it had approved the Asian Development Bank's application to issue Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds worth T$7 billion or about US$255 million.

"The central bank yesterday approved the ADB's application for a T$7 billion issue," a central bank spokesman told Reuters by telephone. The spokesman declined to give details, saying only that the decision was taken on Wednesday.
Lead underwriter Chinatrust Bank said the ADB applied to the central bank last week to issue US$200-260 million in Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds in early December.

Chinatrust spokeswoman Wang Li told Reuters that other details such as the exact issue date or term of the bonds have yet to be made final, but she said the issue likely would have a term of seven or 10 years.
The ADB initially had envisaged a June launch for a 10-year, US$200 million issue, but it later postponed the issue without giving a reason.

The December issue would be ADB's second issue denominated in Taiwan dollars and reflects a drive by Taiwan's government to encourage international agencies to raise capital in the island's cash-flush money market.
Central bank and finance ministry officials have said the ADB's bond issues would help internationalise Taiwan's bond market and raise the credibility of Taiwan's currency.
In August 1995, the ADB issued a seven-year Taiwan dollar-denominated bond valued at T$2.6 billion, or roughly US$100 million.
